# Migrations are generated by drizzle-kit and applied by Drizzle's own migrator

Database changes are plain SQL files in `apps/api/migrations/`. `drizzle-kit generate` writes them by comparing the `*.tables.ts` files with the last snapshot, and a person reads each file before committing. They are applied by `bun run db:migrate`, a small script around Drizzle's built-in migrator that holds a Postgres advisory lock (so two copies can't run at once) and applies all new files in one transaction. It runs as its own release step, never when the app starts.

We looked at dbmate (a simple standalone runner), Atlas (schema diffing with checks for destructive changes) and graphile-migrate (a Postgres-only, hand-written SQL workflow). All three are good, but each adds a second tool next to the one that already writes our SQL, and dbmate and graphile-migrate would lose the automatic diff from the table files. Drizzle's migrator ships inside `drizzle-orm`, which the app already uses, so the release image needs nothing extra.

## Consequences

- Migrations only go forward; there are no "down" files. A bad change is fixed with a new migration, which fits the two-release rule for removing columns.
- SQL that Drizzle can't express, such as the `EXCLUDE` constraint that stops overlapping bookings, goes in a hand-written file: `cd apps/api && bunx drizzle-kit generate --custom --name <name>`.
- All pending files run in one transaction, so `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` can't be used. If a large table ever needs it, that index is created by hand outside the migrator.
- Two branches that both add a migration conflict in `migrations/meta/_journal.json`. The second one to merge deletes its file and runs `bun run db:generate` again.
- pg-boss keeps its own tables in the `pgboss` schema and upgrades them itself when the app starts.
- Drizzle 1.0, still in beta, changes the migration folder layout; moving to it later is a one-time upgrade.
